message.content:
The three most widely‑recognized “great” schisms in Christian history are:

| # | Schism | Approximate Date | Key Parties & Outcome |
|---|--------|------------------|-----------------------|
| 1 | **Great Schism (East–West Schism)** | 1054 CE | Split between the Eastern (Byzantine) Church and the Western (Roman) Church, leading to the formation of the Eastern Orthodox and Roman Catholic Churches. |
| 2 | **Protestant Reformation** | 1517–1648 CE | Break from the Roman Catholic Church initiated by figures such as Martin Luther, John Calvin, and others, resulting in the creation of Lutheran, Reformed, Anglican, and other Protestant denominations. |
| 3 | **East–West Schism (Second Great Schism)** | 1965 CE | Often called the “Second Great Schism,” this refers to the formal separation of the Eastern Orthodox Church from the Oriental Orthodox Churches (e.g., Coptic, Armenian, Syriac) over Christological disputes, solidifying the division that had existed since the Council of Chalcedon (451 CE). |

These three events are typically cited as the major turning points that divided the Christian world into distinct, enduring traditions.
